aka Merge Queen and casual games strategist, bringing you insights shaped by years of professional Game Design experience and learnings from smash merge hits like Travel Town.
For years, I’ve been following the gaming industry, and one of my favorite things to track is new game releases.
New games do more than just introduce new competitors. They often predict future trends, bring innovation, and show off creative mechanics. Most importantly, they give me insights into what the "next big thing" might be.
I invite you to follow me here!
I’ll be sharing bite-sized, insightful posts about interesting new games, why they matter, and my personal take on them.This past May brought us several intriguing titles. However, one that truly stands out is
Just Desserts
, a new soft-launch title from Chinese gaming giant
Century Games
, better known for the most successful strategy games, Whiteout Survivals & Kingshot.
Merge 2 Crash Course
View fullsize
For those unfamiliar with the
Merge
genre, here is a quick catch-up: this genre has skyrocketed in popularity over the last few years, becoming the
2nd highest-grossing
in the casual genre after match-3. Furthermore, it has shown phenomenal year-over-year growth, and it’s not slowing down anytime soon.
View fullsize
Right now, the undisputed king of the genre is
Gossip Harbor
(from Chinese
Microfun
), which has comfortably cemented its spot as one of the Top 5 highest-grossing mobile games globally.
To give you a quick, no-nonsense crash course on how we got here: Gossip Harbor actually started as a game heavily inspired by Love & Pies (from Trailmix, a Supercell studio). But in a classic student-surpasses-the-master twist, it outworked and evolved into a fierce competitor that has left everyone else in the dust.
But market growth alone doesn’t explain why Merge 2 has become such a powerful genre. To understand what makes these games so engaging, and why the formula has proven so scalable, we need to look under the hood at the core gameplay loop that drives the experience.
The Core Gameplay Loop
The core gameplay loop takes place on a board filled with Producers and orders that give players clear goals to work toward. Players tap Producers to generate items, then merge two items of the same type to progressively reach the items required by orders. Each tap consumes Energy, making it the resource that powers the core loop.Completing these orders rewards players with resources, enables progression, and ultimately allows them to renovate and develop the Meta, the space where the game’s narrative unfolds.
While the board provides the moment-to-moment gameplay, the Meta and its narrative give that gameplay a larger purpose. Players are not simply merging items for the sake of merging, they are completing orders for the characters they have become invested in, using their progress to unlock new areas, advance the story, and see what happens next.The interesting part is that the merge loop doesn’t exist in isolation. While the board provides the actions that keep players busy, the Meta gives those actions meaning. This connection between gameplay and narrative is one of the key reasons Merge 2 games can turn a relatively simple mechanic into such a sticky experience.
Narrative as a Retention Driver
Narrative plays a critical role in the overall experience and is one of the key drivers bringing players back to the game. This is particularly relevant in the Merge 2 genre, where the majority of the audience is female and emotional investment in characters can become a powerful engagement driver.
Love & Pies
is one of the strongest examples of this approach. The game established a highly engaging cast of distinctive characters and built a compelling narrative around them, helping it achieve exceptionally strong retention within the genre. Its approach to character-driven storytelling has since become an important benchmark for many Merge 2 titles that followed, including
Gossip Harbor
.
Importantly, the narrative characters are not disconnected from the core gameplay. They are also the characters requesting orders on the board. This creates a direct relationship between the two layers of the game: the characters provide the motivation, while the board provides the activity through which players help them. Players are effectively “working for” these characters, transforming each merge and completed order into a small contribution toward the larger story.
The “One More Merge” Effect
A major part of what makes the Merge 2 loop so compelling is the
perception of constant, achievable progress
.
Every order is broken down into smaller merging steps, creating a clear path toward completion. As players get closer to the requested item, the goal feels increasingly attainable- often creating the feeling that they are “just one more merge” away.
This creates a powerful progression illusion: the player is continuously moving forward, but there is always another small step within reach. That combination of visible progress, achievable goals, and incomplete tasks makes disengagement surprisingly difficult.
The board itself reinforces this behavior. Players are constantly balancing several micro-goals at once as they find themselves caught in an almost endless OCD-like loop: generating items, merging, completing orders, freeing up board space, and organizing their inventory. This creates a highly satisfying optimization loop in which players naturally want to “clean up” the board before stopping.
In other words, the game is not only asking players to progress,it is constantly giving them something that feels almost finished.
